name: LinkedIn Profile Analysis - Frontend Developer
description: Signals extracted from LinkedIn profiles to evidence Frontend Developer skills. LinkedIn provides professional context, endorsements, and career trajectory data.

sections.notes: Self-described; provides intent and self-assessment context. Look for framework specialization signals (e.g., 'Senior React Developer' vs generic 'Frontend Developer').

sections.description: Work experience entries with job titles, companies, and descriptions.
sections.notes: Similar to CV work experience but often more concise. Look for frontend-specific job titles and descriptions.
quality_indicators: Frontend-specific job titles (Frontend Engineer, UI Developer, React Developer, Full-Stack with frontend focus)
Company type (product company vs agency — different skill depth signals)

sections.description: Skills listed with endorsement counts from connections.
sections.notes: Endorsements have very low evidential value — they are exchanged socially. However, the skill list provides self-reported skill claims.
Same as CV certifications — theoretical knowledge indicator, not practical proof.

sections.description: Projects section with descriptions and links.
sections.notes: Provides additional project context. Links to GitHub or live demos increase strength.

sections.description: Written recommendations from colleagues or managers.
sections.notes: Third-party validation. Look for specific mentions of frontend technologies or architectural contributions.

sections.description: Technical posts and articles published on LinkedIn.
sections.notes: Indicates thought leadership and depth. Frontend-specific blog posts about performance, architecture, or framework internals are strong signals.

signal_mapping.description: How LinkedIn mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Job experience explicitly describing React/Vue/Angular SPA development
Job experience describing Next.js or Nuxt SSR applications
Job experience describing accessibility compliance or WCAG audits
Job experience describing performance optimization with metrics
Job experience describing design system or component library development
Technical article about frontend architecture or framework internals
Endorsement for 'Web Performance' or 'Core Web Vitals'

important_notes: ALL extracted signals MUST be mapped to COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id})
LinkedIn data supplements but should not override GitHub or assessment evidence
Endorsements have near-zero evidential value on their own
Job titles can be inflated — 'Senior Frontend Architect' at a 3-person startup differs from the same title at a FAANG
Career trajectory (progression from junior to mid to senior frontend roles) provides useful context
Look for technical content creation (posts, articles) about frontend topics as evidence of deep understanding
Framework-specific job titles ('React Developer') are stronger signals than generic ones ('Web Developer')
